articles.title: Announcers for Colts vs. Ravens Week 1 matchup revealed
articles.summary: The announcers for the Colts vs. Ravens Week 1 matchup have been revealed.
articles.body:
The announcers for the Indianapolis Colts' Week 1 matchup have been revealed .

The Colts will open the 2026 regular season at home against the Baltimore Ravens . Kickoff on Sunday, Sept. 13, will be at 1:00 PM ET.

Who are the announcers for Colts vs. Ravens in Week 1?

The game will be aired on CBS, with Andrew Catalon, Logan Ryan, and AJ Ross on the call.

Week 1 is the start of what is expected to be a difficult stretch to open up the 2026 season for the Colts. Matchups with Kansas City and Houston await Indianapolis in Weeks 2 and 3.

It will also be Daniel Jones' first live game since Week 14 of last season, when he suffered an Achilles injury.

The Colts can be an easy team to doubt, but there is a lot to like about this roster. Daniel Jones is healthy, and around him is what should be a stout offensive line unit and plenty of playmaking potential.

Defensively, Indianapolis should have a very good secondary, and a front that features DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and Laiatu Latu.

That said, the depth at a number of positions is in question, and whether or not the Colts have enough pass-rush juice at defensive end around Latu remains to be seen.

articles.title: FSU football's winners and losers from ACC opening loss
articles.summary: Florida State forced four turnovers but could not capitalize enough in a 27-24 loss to SMU. See the winners and losers from the game.
articles.body:
Florida State had every opportunity to steal a marquee ACC win Monday night. The SMU Mustangs refused to let the Seminoles finish the job .

The No. 19 Mustangs overcame four turnovers, including two interceptions from quarterback Kevin Jennings and a muffed punt that Florida State recovered deep in SMU territory, to escape Doak Campbell Stadium with a 27-24 victory on Nick Reed's 20-yard field goal with 21 seconds remaining. FSU forced two fumbles and two interceptions, yet turned those four takeaways into only seven points.

Here are the biggest winners and losers from Florida State's ACC-opening loss.

Kromah continues to look like the centerpiece of Florida State's offense.

The sophomore followed his 115-yard performance against New Mexico State by setting a new career high with 116 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. His 54-yard run in the second quarter set up a field goal, while his six-yard touchdown in the third tied the game at 17. Kromah became the first FSU player with consecutive 100-yard rushing games since Trey Benson in 2022.

Two interceptions cannot erase 430 passing yards allowed and several busted coverages.

Jennings consistently found explosive plays against the Seminoles, including touchdown passes of 50 and 79 yards. SMU finished with four receivers over 70 yards and averaged 8.7 yards per offensive play despite turning the ball over four times.

Winner: Florida State's ability to create turnovers

FSU's defense had plenty of problems, but generating takeaways was not one of them.

Quindarrius Jones forced and recovered a fumble on SMU's opening possession, Nehemiah Chandler intercepted Jennings in the end zone, Gemari Sands recovered a muffed punt and Ashlynd Barker added another fourth-quarter interception. Four takeaways should normally be enough to put a team in position to win.

The frustrating part for Florida State was what happened afterward.

One problem from the New Mexico State game followed Florida State directly into Week 1.

The Seminoles finished an ugly 2-for-15 on third down, repeatedly forcing their defense back onto the field and failing to capitalize on SMU mistakes. The contrast was significant, with the Mustangs converting 8 of 14 third downs.

FSU had four extra possessions created by turnovers and still managed only 324 total yards.

The contrast between these programs has become increasingly difficult to ignore.

Entering Monday night, SMU was 14-2 in ACC regular-season play since joining the conference in 2024, while Florida State was 3-13 over that same two-season span. The Mustangs' victory moved those records to 15-2 for SMU and 3-14 for FSU since the start of 2024.

The loss also dropped Norvell to 22-27 in ACC play during his Florida State tenure and marked FSU's third consecutive loss in a conference opener.

articles.title: “A struggle”: Paul Scholes says Carrick has a massive Matheus Cunha headache brewing
articles.summary: 1 Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has warned Michael Carrick that he may have a major problem on his hands with Matheus Cunha.StrugglingSeveral United...
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has warned Michael Carrick that he may have a major problem on his hands with Matheus Cunha.

Several United players underperformed in Sunday's stalemate with Everton, but Cunha was the worst of the lot.

From overhit passes and heavy touches to poor positional awareness and glaring misses, his performance was a catalogue of errors. There was simply too much that went wrong.

In yet another game, Cunha didn't appear to have a clear role in the team. Last term, Carrick primarily used him on the left of the attack. But Marcus Rashford's return has seen him pushed elsewhere in the team.

Carrick appears to favour Rashford out wide, meaning Cunha has been deployed up front, in something of a false nine role, although sometimes Bruno Fernandes has assumed that role, with Cunha dropping into the 10.

The Brazilian has somewhat looked lost and lacking the inspiration and confidence he was oozing in his maiden campaign at Old Trafford. It's still early stages and he may still be getting up to full fitness but Scholes thinks Carrick has a dilemma on his hands.

The former England international said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast , "It's very difficult to watch a Man United team without a centre forward."

"Now, what Cunha is, I don't really know what Cunha is, what is he a number 10 or a wide player."

"But he's definitely not a number nine. And watching the United team without a number nine, it's a struggle."

When Benjamin Sesko was introduced at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he looked much better and found the back of the net to temporarily restore United's lead.

The Slovenian rose highest to head home a superb cross from Luke Shaw before Ainsley Maitland-Niles broke the hearts of the travelling supporters with a stoppage-time stunner.

It will be interesting to see Carrick's selection when United face Sabah in their Champions League opener on Thursday.

articles.title: Lyon’s sporting director reveals why they chose Openda over Benzema
articles.summary: Karim Benzema is a free agent after his Al Hilal contract was terminated, and he wanted one last opportunity in European football by returning to his former...
articles.body:
Karim Benzema is a free agent after his Al Hilal contract was terminated, and he wanted one last opportunity in European football by returning to his former club, Lyon.

The Ligue 1 side were looking for a striker after Endrick returned to Real Madrid following his loan spell at the club, and signing Benzema made sense given his experience. Benzema also wanted the move to happen and was prepared for a return, but Lyon ultimately chose a different option.

Lyon signed Lois Openda on loan from Juventus , and Benzema never returned to the club. The French side were more than happy to land Openda and will hope he performs well for them, while Juve will also want him to succeed so they can either sign him permanently or have the opportunity to sell him.

Benzema's return to Europe was also complicated by clauses in his Saudi Pro League contract, which tie him to some off-field work in the country beyond his playing spell there. Those contractual obligations contributed to the difficulties surrounding a potential return to Lyon.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Lyon sporting director Matthieu Louis Jean has now spoken about the two deals and explained why Benzema did not return, as quoted by Calciomercato :

"It's almost a fantasy. There was contact with an intermediary this summer. It didn't go any further: it was impossible due to contractual issues."

He added: "We didn't go any further because we needed a fast attacker and we were working on Openda."

Lyon therefore decided to focus their efforts on Openda rather than pursue a return for Benzema. Although the experienced striker was interested in rejoining his former club, contractual complications prevented the move from progressing.

For Benzema, the situation means his hoped for return to European football with Lyon did not materialise. For the French side, meanwhile, Openda became their preferred solution in attack, with the club now hoping the Juventus loanee can deliver enough quality to justify a potential permanent deal.

articles.title: Former Gunner has contract terminated by Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Edu Gaspar’s contract with Nottingham Forest has finally been terminated, six months after the decision was made to part ways with the former Arsenal man.Pho...
articles.body:
Edu Gaspar's contract with Nottingham Forest has finally been terminated, six months after the decision was made to part ways with the former Arsenal man.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Paul Taylor reported for The Athletic on Monday night that Edu Gaspar has officially left Nottingham Forest , with sources close to the club claiming the former Gunner's contract has been terminated.

Edu was working for Forest as their global head of football, but he didn't last long in the position. He was only officially appointed in July 2025, and by March 2026, reports suggested an internal decision had been made to part ways.

It took a long time for those reports to come to fruition, and The Athletic claim there's no expectation Forest will ever announce the departure in an official statement. But he's already been replaced via internal promotions.

Tom Hamilton reports for ESPN that Edu didn't play an active role in Forest's summer transfer window, which is unsurprising considering reports in March suggested he'd been told to stay away from the club and the training ground. Officially, Edu's last day in his role was last week.

Edu had initially signed a five-year deal with Forest, but the club held doubts about the director's long-term future following his clash with manager Nuno Espirito Santo last year.

Despite Nuno's departure, Edu's presence at the club remained a contentious issue behind the scenes.

Edu pushed for the signings of Douglas Luiz and former Gunner Omari Hutchinson last year, whilst Nuno and the recruitment team wanted other players. Luiz left the club in January, and Hutchinson is currently out on loan.

Edu was also key in the loan signing of Oleksandr Zinchenko from Arsenal , which did not go well at all. Zinchenko didn't even finish the season before leaving for Ajax .

Forest had a poor season, finishing 16th, and Edu appears to have taken a lot of the blame for that. This contract termination has been an inevitability for a long time now.

articles.title: Liverpool now considering deal for African star
articles.summary: This summer, it felt like Liverpool were being linked with a new player almost every day. The Anfield outfit had a lot of changes that needed to be made to t...
articles.body:
This summer, it felt like Liverpool were being linked with a new player almost every day.

The Anfield outfit had a lot of changes that needed to be made to their ranks and, while some were made, it still feels like they're a bit behind their title rivals.

For example, both Manchester City and Chelsea spent an absolute fortune on new players this summer and, while Liverpool may have splashed around £123 million on Bradley Barcola , his arrival was nothing in comparison.

Obviously, thanks to Barcola's arrival, on paper, Liverpool now have one of the best attacks in the world.

However, since Mohamed Salah is gone and the Reds still haven't replaced him with a natural right-winger, there's still a high chance that another attacker could be brought in over the next year or so.

So, the fact that the Reds are keeping their door open to new arrivals makes a lot of sense.

Liverpool could try and make another move for Ismaila Sarr in January

Throughout the summer, Liverpool's main goal seemed to be strengthening their attack.

Many different attackers were linked but, in the end, only two were signed.

Most people thought that an entire rebuild of Liverpool's attack was on the cards but, since they don't have an endless bucket of money to spend, that was far from the case.

So, even though the Reds' main focus was on improving their forward line, it now seems like their January transfer window could also be focused on bringing another attacker or two in.

That is, if a report from Football Insider is to be believed.

"Liverpool will consider making another move to sign Ismaila Sarr in January after failing to agree a deal before the summer deadline, sources have told Football Insider," they shared.

"Sarr was a target for the Reds throughout the transfer window after impressing for Crystal Palace over the last few seasons.

"Andoni Iraola wanted to add quality and depth to his attacking ranks following Mo Salah's departure.

"Bradley Barcola arrived in a move worth £120million before the deadline, and they remained hot on the trail of Sarr but failed to get a deal done.

"Sarr still wants to join Liverpool and he will stay on their radar in the months to come."

Liverpool must make sure they get a good deal for Ismaila Sarr if they sign him

Obviously, Sarr has plenty of Premier League experience and, since that's one of the main things that Liverpool are missing at the moment, a move for the Senegal international makes a lot of sense.

But, since he's 28 years old and has never scored more than nine Premier League goals in a season before, the £70 million + that Crystal Palace were demanding for him this summer felt rather steep.

However, if Liverpool really do want to sign the winger and do end up trying to get a deal for him over the line in summer, they must ensure that they get value for their money.

A fee around £50 million would be much more reasonable but, because of how big Liverpool are as a club and how desperately they need a right-winger, any attacker that they try and sign is going to be extortionately priced.

So, the best thing for them to do is just to see how things pan out and then re-evaluate in January, otherwise, they could end up making a deal that they end up regretting in six months and, since the Reds have already spent so much money over the last couple of transfer windows, that would be far from ideal.

articles.title: What the Patriots jersey you wear says about you in 2026
articles.summary: A rundown of some of the most common Patriots jerseys out in the wild, and what it says about the fan who chose to buy it.
articles.body:
For football fans, a team jersey is more than just a piece of clothing. It's a personality test that reveals a lot about the wearer as a person.

For New England Patriots fans, the choice of which player's jersey is worth spending upwards of $200 on is a big one. Typically, it reflects what kind of fan that person is.

So here's a rundown of some of the most common Patriots jerseys out in the wild, and what it says about the fan who chose to buy it.

Drake Maye, No. 10 — Have you said out loud that you love Drake Maye more than you've said it about your loved ones? The fact that you have to stop and think about it is troubling.

Mac Jones, No. 10 — You're weighing the pros and cons of being someone who covers up the name with duct tape.

Bailey Zappe, No. 4 — You held out hope deep into 2023 that Zappe was actually the guy.

Christian Gonzalez, No. 0 — You'd like to politely tell the Patriots to "JUST PAY THE MAN."

Ty Law, No. 24 — You'd like to tell the Patriots that you agree with the fan in the Gonzo jersey.

TreVeyon Henderson, No. 32 — You're worried about Rhamondre Stevenson stealing carries and diminishing Henderson's fantasy value.

Hunter Henry, No. 85 — Every time the offense gets to the 10-yard line, you say, "Here comes the play action."

Julian Edelman, No. 11 — You also own at least one of the following jerseys: Brad Marchand, Dustin Pedroia, Rajon Rondo.

Stefon Diggs, No. 8 — In the past year, you learned more about Cardi B than you ever expected to.

Antonio Brown, No. 17 — You refuse to admit this was a bad purchase and now use it to get a rise out of people at parties.

David Andrews, No. 60 — So, what brand of truck do you drive?

Tom Brady, No. 12 — When someone orders a bunch of pizzas, you're the one who will order a cheese pizza, even when others say it's "boring." You smile to yourself when the cheese pizza is the first one that's eaten.

One of those off-brand Tom Brady jerseys that's, like, black or camo — You scoffed at ordering the cheese pizza. But now that it's here, you're absolutely grabbing two slices.

Tedy Bruschi, No. 54 — You went to training camp this year and thought to yourself, "Practices are so soft these days."

Mike Vrabel, No. 50 — You used to have a great, underrated jersey. Now you just get a lot of bad Dianna Russini jokes.

Randy Moss, No. 18 — You've been waiting for this team to trade for a top-tier receiver for years and were ecstatic when they landed A.J. Brown.

A.J. Brown, No. 1 — You're really hoping this purchase doesn't turn out like your Stefon Diggs or Antonio Brown jerseys.

Rob Gronkowski, No. 87 — You've been politely asked to leave after you Gronk-spiked something that isn't a football at a public gathering.

Steve Grogan, No. 14 — People think the Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks was bad? You're ready to educate them about the '85 Bears.

Drew Bledsoe, No. 11 — You think fans in the luxury boxes are wimps who could never last 30 seconds on the cold metal bleachers at the old Foxboro Stadium.

Matthew Judon, No. 9 — There was a period of time where you thought he was the best pass rusher on the planet and should have gotten a bajillion dollars.

Matthew Slater, No. 18 — You clap politely for opposing teams instead of booing. It's just good sportsmanship.

Rhamondre Stevenson, No. 38 — You're constantly defending Stevenson as a lead running back and reminding people how good he was in 2022.

Troy Brown, No. 80 — You have rewatched at least one of the 2001-2004 Super Bowls at some point this year.

Rodney Harrison, No. 37 — Whenever a player gets flagged for a hit to the head, you yell, "What's he supposed to do there?!"

Matt Light, No. 72 — You scan the crowd around you during the national anthem to check if everyone has taken off their hats.

Devin McCourty, No. 32 — You were the one person at the bar actually watching the second half of the preseason game on the TVs.

John Hannah, No. 73 — You're overcome with an indescribable sense of despair when you have to tell other Patriots fans whose jersey you're wearing.

Tommy DeVito, No. 16 — You know all the best Italian restaurants in a 10-mile radius of your house.

Ben Coates, No. 87 — Older fans look at you and give a subtle, knowing nod.

articles.title: Baker relishing role in Walker Cup victory
articles.summary: Eliot Baker says helping Great Britain and Ireland win the Walker Cup still has not sunk in.
articles.body:
Eliot Baker says helping Great Britain and Ireland win the Walker Cup still has not sunk in.

The 23-year-old from Devon helped his side produce the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States 13½-12½.

Baker beat experienced United States player Stewart Hagestad on the final hole of his singles match as GB&I overturned a three-point deficit going into the final individual round.

"I was in a complete state of shock for about 20 minutes until we actually lifted the trophy," he told BBC South West.

"It still kind of felt like the trophy was going to be going to them. I think just deep down it was almost what was expected with the scoreline going into the final session.

"But I'm sure over the next couple of days it will truly sink in."

The victory was Baker's only win of the competition, having halved the opening morning's foursomes and losing in the second morning's foursomes 3&2 with team-mate Stuart Grehan, but it proved to be vital.

"That is the highlight of my career, for sure," he added.

"Winning - that feeling was unbelievable. It'll take a long time to come down from that, but that is the pinnacle of amateur golf so it takes a lot to beat it."

Baker's win came in his second appearance at the Walker Cup, but it is likely to be his last.

He is planning on taking up golf full-time, meaning he will no longer be eligible for the amateur competition.

"I should hopefully be turning pro fairly soon," he said.

"As long as all things go well over the next month or so I should be turning pro and hopefully heading out on to the DP World Tour.

"But it's a little bit of a waiting game to see, but everything's in a good position so far."

articles.title: Trevor Story’s Blunt Message Helps Jarren Duran End Negative Spiral
articles.summary: Trevor Story challenged Jarren Duran to end his negative self-talk before the Red Sox outfielder delivered a two-hit performance against the Angels.
articles.body:
Jarren Duran changed his appearance before changing the direction of his September. The Boston Red Sox outfielder cut his signature long hair during the team's weekend series in Baltimore, dyed it blond and then delivered one of his best offensive performances in months.

Duran went 2-for-4 with a home run and a double in Boston's 5-2 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Monday at Fenway Park. His solo shot was his 20th home run of the season and helped the Red Sox extend their winning streak to five games.

The new look created plenty of attention. A direct message from Trevor Story might have been considerably more important.

Trevor Story Challenges Duran's Negative Self-Talk

Duran has openly acknowledged his frustration throughout a season that has not always matched his expectations. Story, whose locker has been located next to Duran's for years, eventually decided his teammate needed to hear a difficult truth.

"He finally heard it enough in Baltimore," Duran said. "He's like, 'Dude, that's enough. All this negative self-talk, you're just making it a reality instead of if I talk positive, then positive outcomes will come.'"

Isiah Kiner-Falefa delivered a similar message.

Rather than allowing Duran to remain consumed by his season-long numbers, Kiner-Falefa encouraged him to focus on getting hot for Boston's postseason push.

That shift in perspective appeared to help Monday.

Duran homered in the second inning and added a double in the fifth, recording multiple extra-base hits in the same game for the first time since May 20.

That honesty has followed Duran throughout his Red Sox career. His intensity can help make him an electrifying player, but it also can turn every difficult at-bat into something larger than one out. Story recognized that pattern and challenged him to interrupt it.

Red Sox Need Duran Focused On September Opportunity

Duran's 2026 season has not completely followed the path he imagined, but it remains far from a failure. His 20th home run moved him within reach of a 20-home run, 20-stolen base season. Red Sox manager Chad Tracy also noted that Duran still has a legitimate opportunity to finish with more than 80 RBIs.

Those milestones would represent significant production, even if Duran believes he should have delivered more. Boston needs him thinking about what remains possible.

The Red Sox improved to 80-65 with Monday's victory and moved 15 games above .500 for the first time this season. They also remained within striking distance of the New York Yankees in the American League playoff race.

October could provide Duran with an opportunity to change the entire perception of his season. A productive postseason would matter considerably more than the frustrating stretches that preceded it. The Red Sox do not need Duran replaying every missed opportunity from April through August.

They need the aggressive, disruptive player capable of changing a game with his power and speed.

Duran's haircut gave his teammates something to joke about.

Story's message gave him something more valuable to consider.

The Red Sox veteran reminded Duran that repeating negative thoughts can turn frustration into a permanent expectation. Monday's performance showed what can happen when Duran gives himself permission to move forward. One strong game does not guarantee a September surge. It might be exactly where one begins.

USL Dunkerque are reported to have reached a verbal agreement with M'Baye Niang (31) on a one-year contract with an option for a further year, according to L'Équipe .

A free agent since leaving Turkish club Gençlerbirliği SK, where he played and proved decisive on eight occasions (six goals, two assists) in 27 appearances last season, the Senegalese striker is reportedly open to a return to France.

Having come through the SM Caen academy and played for Montpellier HSC, Stade Rennais, Girondins de Bordeaux and AJ Auxerre, Niang has made over 160 appearances and scored around 40 goals in Ligue 1.

A Senegal international (23 caps, four goals), the Meulan-born player also boasts significant international experience, having previously played for AC Milan, Watford and Torino, amongst others.

Having secured the services of Steven Nzonzi (37) this summer, USLD could well be set to pull off another major coup to round off their transfer window.

articles.title: 'Pray': Arizona State HC Kenny Dillingham on facing QB Marcel Reed
articles.summary: Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham had a simple answer when asked how to game plan for Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed: “Pray.”
articles.body:
Texas A&M and Arizona State University share a lot of mutual respect, with both teams speaking highly of each other ahead of their Week 2 matchup on Saturday.

One of the more interesting comments from both Mike Elko and ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham concerned Aggies QB Marcel Reed. Several national pundits believe A&M can only go as far as Reed can take them, and most share the same criticism—accuracy, especially on deep throws. However, both coaches praised Reed and do not believe he gets enough credit for what he's done and how much better he's gotten over time.

Coach Elko pointed out that while Reed does get a lot of blame, he is 12-1 as a regular-season starter over the last two years and has played very well overall . Coach Dillingham, on the other hand, had a much more comical response when asked about game planning for Marcel Reed.

After that quick joke, he went on to explain what makes Reed difficult to game plan for, and he put a lot of emphasis on how much more comfortable Reed looks in the pocket and how his touch on passes to all areas of the field has improved.

So, while certain people around and outside of Aggieland might not be as high on Reed as others, two of the top coaches in the country believe that Reed should get a little more credit for what he's been able to do up to this point.

articles.title: Daniel Farke: We want to go through

articles.body:
Daniel Farke will take his side away from home on Wednesday evening, facing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in Round Three of the EFL Cup.

The Whites have been a familiar opponent of the Blues in cup competitions over recent seasons, as well as the league, which have all been well-contested and hard fought encounters.

Speaking to the media ahead of Wednesday night's 8pm kick-off, the boss gave his thoughts on our latest encounter in West London.

He said: "We try to win it. That is a topic, the quickest way to Europe and to some glory.

"Of course, knowing that the Premier League always will have the priority and to make sure that we are as successful as possible there, and especially to reach our first goal, to establish ourselves on this level.

"We are not the favourites to win the EFL Cup. We know this also [will be a] challenging, difficult game. But of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid.

"At this stage of the campaign, of course, you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players.

"That is also important but, nevertheless, we want to be at our best and if possible we also want to go through into the next round."

Discussing the opposition, Farke added: "They have been stronger than they were last year. I judge more or less also like the offence, how they play with Pedro, with Palmer, with Rogers.

"There are not many teams in Europe who have such a quality. And also, if you look at the options on the bench, it is outstanding quality.

"So, they definitely have a top manager and also top players but we are looking at ourselves, and we also want to be competitive. We travel respectful but also not in fear. We want to go through into the next round."
